title: My new town has one rule on the first snow. Light a lantern for everyone inside.
transcript:
My new town has one rule on the first snow. Light a lantern for everyone inside. Three slow knocks shook my front door, an hour after the first snow started.

I'd moved in that week. The woman at the post office told me the rule twice. First snow, everybody stays in. One lantern in the window for every person in the house. "It counts," she said. "Don't make it count wrong."

The realtor had laughed about it. He said the last owner always lit two, for company. Funny, since he lived alone too. So I lit one. I set it in the front window and turned off every other light.

Then the knocking came again. Three more. Slower. Something dragged along the siding, window to window, like a hand reading the house.

"How many?" a voice asked. Flat. Patient. Right outside the glass.

I didn't answer. The lantern flame leaned toward the window, like the cold was breathing on it.

Then it laughed, soft and pleased. "Two lanterns," it said. "Two inside. Goodnight."

Footsteps crunched away into the trees. I finally let my breath out.

Then I noticed warm light spilling down the stairs, from the upstairs window.

I only lit one.
